rawInput.message:
DIGEST: lease.txt and notice.txt (both plain-text copies; they carry line numbers, not page numbers, so references below are to clause or paragraph numbers)

lease.txt
- Type: commercial lease, dated 3 March 2025. Labelled "invented test document" at line 1.
- Parties: Landlord Halvard Quince Properties Ltd, 12 Orrin Lane, Pemberton. Tenant Mirelle Dask Bakery Ltd, Unit 4, Tarrow Arcade, Pemberton.
- Execution: signed "H. Quince (for the Landlord)" and "M. Dask (for the Tenant)", witness Corin Abbet (lines 40-42). Signed-by-whom authority is not shown.
- Premises (cl. 1.1-1.2): Unit 4 including rear store room, excluding the yard.
- Term (cl. 2.1): 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2030. Tenant break on 31 March 2028 on six months' written notice (cl. 2.2), so notice must be served by about 30 September 2027. Exact service date is not stated.
- Rent (cl. 3.1): 24,000 per year, monthly in advance on the 1st (2,000 per month). Currency not stated.
- Late interest (cl. 3.2): 4% above base rate on rent unpaid 14 days after due date. Base rate is not defined.
- Rent review (cl. 3.3): upward only, on 1 April 2027.
- Deposit (cl. 4.1-4.2): 6,000 on signing, returned within 30 days after term ends, less lawful deductions.
- Repairs (cl. 5.1-5.3): Tenant keeps interior in repair. Landlord repairs roof, structure and common parts. Landlord must start roof repairs within 21 days of written notice of a defect.
- Use (cl. 6.1-6.2): bakery with retail counter only; no baking 23:00-05:00.
- Forfeiture (cl. 7.1-7.2): re-entry if rent is 21 days in arrears after written demand; re-entry needs 14 days' prior written notice to Tenant.
- Notices (cl. 8.1): in writing, by hand or recorded post, to the addresses above. Email is not a permitted method.

notice.txt
- Type: notice of arrears and intended re-entry, dated 2 September 2025, from the Landlord to the Tenant.
- Delivery: "by hand" (header). A footer note (line 33) says a copy went "by email only to the Tenant's accountant". That is not a cl. 8.1 method and not service on the Tenant.
- Signed: Halvard Quince, Director (line 31).
- Arrears (paras 2-5): 2,000 each for 1 July, 1 August and 1 September 2025, total 6,000. Consistent with cl. 3.1.
- Interest claimed (para 6) at 4% above base rate under cl. 3.2.
- Para 7 says the letter is a written demand for cl. 7.1.
- Para 8: re-entry threatened unless arrears paid within 7 days. Cl. 7.2 requires 14 days' prior written notice, so the 7-day period looks shorter than the lease allows.
- Paras 9-11: Landlord says the yard is used for flour-sack storage, cites cl. 1.2 that the yard is not part of the Premises, and demands clearance within 7 days. This is internally inconsistent: the lease gives no yard obligation, so the Landlord's basis for the demand is unclear.
- Para 12: reserves rights, including to keep the deposit. Cl. 4.2 allows return only after the term ends, less lawful deductions.
- Para 13: payment to "the account on file" (no account details). Para 14: reply to 12 Orrin Lane.

Points for the lawyer
- Current status unknown: the notice is over a year old (today is 24 November 2026). The file shows no response, payment, re-entry, or later correspondence.
- Forfeiture: the 21-day arrears condition (cl. 7.1) and the 14-day notice (cl. 7.2) do not appear to have been met on the face of the notice. The 7-day deadline in para 8 conflicts with cl. 7.2.
- Yard: cl. 1.2 excludes the yard, but para 11 demands clearance. Check whether any other lease term or document covers the yard.
- Service: the notice is "by hand", but the copy to the accountant was sent by email only.
- Rent review 1 April 2027 and break date 31 March 2028 are future events.
- Lease copy is labelled as an invented test document. Confirm it is the executed version before relying on it.

Key quotes
1. "The Premises include the rear store room but not the yard." (lease, cl. 1.2)
2. "Re-entry needs 14 days' prior written notice to the Tenant." (lease, cl. 7.2)
3. "Unless the arrears are paid within 7 days, we intend to re-enter the Premises." (notice, para 8)
4. "This letter is a written demand for the purposes of clause 7.1." (notice, para 7)
5. "Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand or recorded post to the addresses above." (lease, cl. 8.1)

Text copies were readable in full; no garbling noted.

rawInput.message:
DIGEST: reply.txt and order.txt (lease-matter folder). Both text copies read in full. Neither has page markers, so references are to paragraph numbers and file line numbers. Both files label themselves "(invented test document)" in their headers. Confirm whether these are real matter papers before relying on them.

== reply.txt ==
- Type: Tenant's reply to landlord's notice. Dated 8 September 2025, sent by recorded post.
- From: Mirelle Dask Bakery Ltd (tenant). To: Halvard Quince Properties Ltd, 12 Orrin Lane, Pemberton (landlord).
- Execution: signed "Mirelle Dask, Director" (line 30). Not a deed.
- Key facts and positions:
  - Admits July and August 2025 rent unpaid (para 2, line 10).
  - Says September rent paid 1 Sept 2025 by bank transfer, ref MDB-0901 (para 3, line 11). Arrears therefore 4,000, not 6,000 (para 4, line 12).
  - Withholding justified by roof leak from 10 June 2025. Written leak notice given 12 June 2025 (paras 5-6, lines 14-15).
  - Says landlord did not start repairs within 21 days as clause 5.3 requires (para 7, line 16). Clause 5.3 is not in the folder, so this is unverified.
  - Stock loss of 3,150 from water on 2 July 2025 (para 8, line 17). Proposes set-off against arrears (para 13, line 25).
  - Says it will pay the 850 balance once the roof is repaired (para 14, line 26). Note: 4,000 less 3,150 = 850, so the arithmetic is consistent.
  - Says landlord's notice gives 7 days but clause 7.2 requires 14 days' prior written notice before re-entry. Says notice is therefore defective (paras 9-10, lines 19-20). Clause 7.2 is not in the folder.
  - Says flour sacks in yard placed with manager's oral consent in May 2025. Undertakes to move them by 30 September 2025 (paras 11-12, lines 22-23).
  - Warns landlord not to re-enter and threatens an injunction (para 15, line 28).
- Dates and documents referred to but not in the folder: landlord's notice dated 2 September 2025 (para 1, line 8). Clauses 5.3 and 7.2 (lease).
- Inconsistencies:
  - Reply says the notice gave 7 days. The notice itself is not in the folder, so this cannot be checked.
  - Reply's undertaking to clear the yard by 30 Sept 2025 (para 12) differs from the court order's 3 Oct 2025 deadline (order para 4).
  - Reply says the 850 balance will be paid only after roof repair. The court order requires the 4,000 to be paid into court by 17 Oct 2025 (order para 3). That is a different position.

== order.txt ==
- Type: Order of Pemberton County Court, interim injunction. Case no. PC-2025-0417.
- Parties: Claimant Mirelle Dask Bakery Ltd. Defendant Halvard Quince Properties Ltd. District Judge Ombry.
- Date of order: 26 September 2025. Served on both parties by the court on the same date (line 33).
- Execution: court order. The text copy shows no seal or signature block.
- Background: made on the claimant's application dated 19 September 2025 (line 8). Counsel for both parties attended (line 9). That application is not in the folder.
- Orders:
  - Para 1: defendant must not re-enter or change the locks of Unit 4, Tarrow Arcade until trial or further order (line 13).
  - Para 2: defendant must start roof repairs to Unit 4 by 10 October 2025 (line 15).
  - Para 3: claimant must pay 4,000 into court by 17 October 2025 (line 17).
  - Para 4: claimant must clear the yard behind Unit 4 by 3 October 2025 (line 19).
  - Para 5: whether claimant may set off the 3,150 stock loss is reserved to trial (line 21).
  - Para 6: defence due 24 October 2025 (line 23).
  - Para 7: case management hearing 14 November 2025 at 10:00 (line 25).
  - Para 8: costs of the application reserved (line 27).
  - Para 9: if the claimant fails to pay under para 3, para 1 lapses without further order (line 29). This is the key conditional term.
  - Para 10: either party may apply to vary on 48 hours' notice (line 31).

== Points for the lawyer ==
- Today is 24 November 2025? No: today's date is 24 November 2026. Every dated obligation in the order (3 Oct, 10 Oct, 17 Oct, 24 Oct, 14 Nov 2025) has passed. The folder contains no later document, so the current status (payment into court, repairs, trial, set-off ruling, lapse of para 1) is unknown from these two files.
- Check whether the 4,000 was paid by 17 Oct 2025. If not, para 1 lapsed under para 9 and the landlord could have re-entered. This is the most important question.
- Set-off of 3,150 is reserved to trial (para 5). The reply's position on set-off is not decided.
- Clauses 5.3 and 7.2 and the 2 Sept 2025 notice need to be obtained to test the reply's defective-notice argument.

Key quotes (no page numbers in the copies; cited by paragraph and line):
1. "We will pay the balance of 850 once the roof is repaired." (reply.txt, para 14, line 26)
2. "Your notice gives 7 days. Clause 7.2 requires 14 days' prior written notice before re-entry." (reply.txt, para 9, line 19)
3. "The Defendant must not re-enter or change the locks of Unit 4, Tarrow Arcade until trial or further order." (order.txt, para 1, line 13)
4. "If the Claimant fails to pay under paragraph 3, paragraph 1 lapses without further order." (order.txt, para 9, line 29)
5. "The question whether the Claimant may set off the 3,150 stock loss is reserved to trial." (order.txt, para 5, line 21)
